- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase baseline or add upward bias to offset mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction of 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >5% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is bullish and price is below 60% of 30-day high.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to capture momentum.
